questions.question: Explain what a word scale is and describe its main weakness.
questions.expected_answer: A word scale describes the scale in a sentence, such as one centimetre represents one kilometre. Its main weakness is that it is only correct when the map is at its original size. If the map is enlarged, reduced or shown on a screen, one centimetre on the map no longer matches the stated distance.

questions.question: Describe a line scale and explain why it stays correct when a map is photocopied larger.
questions.expected_answer: A line scale is a bar drawn on the map, divided into equal parts, each labelled with the real distance it represents, starting at zero. When the map is enlarged or reduced, the line scale changes size by exactly the same amount, so it still matches the map.

questions.question: One part of a line scale is two centimetres long and labelled ten kilometres. Write this as a word scale and as a ratio scale.
questions.expected_answer: Two centimetres represents ten kilometres, so the word scale is one centimetre represents five kilometres. Five kilometres is five hundred thousand centimetres, so the ratio scale is one to five hundred thousand.
